title: ForgeSight kickoff
raw_text:
ForgeSight kickoff — 14 August 2026, 10:00
Present: Marcus (Head of Product), Priya (Eng Lead), Wei (Design), Tom (Sales). Dana (Customer Success) joined at 10:22.

Marcus (Head of Product): Okay. We're missing Dana, she's on the Northwind renewal, she'll join when she joins. Let's start. ForgeSight. The story we have been telling for two quarters is that an enterprise customer can see their own operational data without filing a request with their own BI team. That is the whole product.
Priya (Eng Lead): And the part we haven't told them is that the prototype takes eleven seconds to draw one bar chart.
Marcus (Head of Product): Which brings me to the first thing, and I want this one written down properly. The first chart on a dashboard must render in under two seconds on our largest customer account. Under two. Not on average.
Priya (Eng Lead): Define largest.
Marcus (Head of Product): Northwind.
Priya (Eng Lead): So that is forty-one million rows in the events table. Two seconds is, I mean, it's doable if we pre-aggregate, but then you're not looking at live data, you're looking at a snapshot of—
Tom (Sales): Sorry, can I — the two seconds, is that the whole page or just the first—
Marcus (Head of Product): First chart. First meaningful chart.
Tom (Sales): Fine. That I can sell.
Wei (Design): Can I do the boring one early, before we get into features? Whatever we build has to work on a tablet. Not a phone. A tablet, held sideways, in a warehouse aisle. Half of Northwind's shift supervisors have never been issued a laptop.
Marcus (Head of Product): Read-only on tablet, or the whole thing?
Wei (Design): Read-only is fine. Dashboards have to be viewable on a tablet in landscape. That's the ask.
Priya (Eng Lead): Noted.
Marcus (Head of Product): Next. Customers keep asking to build their own views, so let's give them that. A customer admin can assemble their own dashboard from a library of widgets, drag and drop, save it, name it. That's table stakes now. Tom, isn't it?
Tom (Sales): It is the first question in every demo. Every single one.
Priya (Eng Lead): Before we go further. Refresh. Are we doing live?
Marcus (Head of Product): Yes. Let's say the data refreshes every thirty seconds. Streaming. If we're selling "see your operations", it has to feel like now.
Priya (Eng Lead): On forty-one million rows. With a two second render budget. And four engineers. By November.
Marcus (Head of Product): ...say the second half of that again.
Priya (Eng Lead): Four engineers. And you told the board the pilot ships end of Q4.
Marcus (Head of Product): The pilot has to be in front of Northwind by the thirtieth of November. That one is fixed, I put it on a slide.
Priya (Eng Lead): Then something goes, and I would rather it was the thirty seconds than the two seconds.

[10:22 — Dana joins]

Dana (Customer Success): Sorry. Renewal ran long. What did I miss?
Marcus (Head of Product): Whether we can stream. Priya thinks not.
Dana (Customer Success): Can I say something about that, because I sit on the tickets. In eighteen months not one customer has asked me for live. Not one. What they ask for constantly is the Monday report. They want the thing emailed to them.
Marcus (Head of Product): Emailed how, exactly?
Dana (Customer Success): A user can schedule a dashboard to be emailed to them as a PDF on a recurring schedule. Weekly, Monday morning, before their own leadership meeting. That request is in thirty-odd tickets, I counted.
Marcus (Head of Product): Right. Then let's reverse the refresh decision. I am withdrawing the thirty seconds. Data refreshes hourly. Hourly is what we build.
Priya (Eng Lead): Thank you.
Marcus (Head of Product): And write it down as hourly, flat, not as a minimum, because somebody will read a minimum as an invitation.
Dana (Customer Success): Two more from the queue while I'm here. People want the numbers out of the thing. Any chart, they want the rows behind it as a CSV.
Priya (Eng Lead): So every chart must let the user export its underlying rows as CSV. Fine. That one is cheap.
Dana (Customer Success): And alerts. Set a threshold on a metric, get told when it's crossed.
Marcus (Head of Product): Told how? Email?
Dana (Customer Success): Email is fine for the pilot. A user can set a threshold on a metric and be notified by email when the metric crosses it.
Tom (Sales): Security, can I? Because this is where I lose deals. Every enterprise buyer asks the same two things. One, do you support our SSO. Two, can I stop a regional manager seeing another region's numbers.
Priya (Eng Lead): One. ForgeSight must authenticate users through the customer's own SAML identity provider, and we store no passwords ourselves. Two is row-level and it is harder.
Tom (Sales): Two is the one that kills deals.
Priya (Eng Lead): Access is scoped by role, so a regional manager only sees rows for their own region. And it has to be enforced in the query, not in the browser, or it isn't enforcement.
Marcus (Head of Product): The audit trail. Meridian asked about that on the security call.
Tom (Sales): Meridian's security review asked for it in writing. Every dashboard view and every export must be written to an audit log we can hand over.
Wei (Design): Branding, before we run out of time. Northwind will not put a dashboard with our logo on it in front of their board. The dashboard has to carry the customer's own logo and colour palette.
Marcus (Head of Product): Agreed. White-label the shell, not the charts.
Priya (Eng Lead): One more from me and it's a constraint, not a wish. We read from the existing warehouse. No second database, no new pipeline. If it isn't in the warehouse it isn't in ForgeSight.
Marcus (Head of Product): For the pilot.
Priya (Eng Lead): For the pilot.
Wei (Design): Last thing, sharing. If I have filtered a dashboard down to one region and one month, I want to send that exact view to a colleague.
Dana (Customer Success): A shareable link that preserves the filters. Yes. That's another ten tickets.
Marcus (Head of Product): In. And what about old data, do we keep it forever?
Priya (Eng Lead): How long do we keep it?
Marcus (Head of Product): I don't know. Thirteen months? Seven years? It depends what Meridian's contract says and I have not read it.
Tom (Sales): I'll find out and come back.
Marcus (Head of Product): Then that one stays open. We're at time. Wei, wireframes by Tuesday.
